harper: Quick RFC follow-up: re model intake gating — tradeoff question. Do we require a fast lightweight probe before a model is ingested into the candidate pool, or accept models immediately and run heavyweight benching async (and quarantine if they fail)? cc @sam @leila

sam: What are the must-have constraints here? i.e. acceptable onboard latency, how many models/day we want to support, and who needs the immediate surface-level metrics?

harper: Constraints: we want <24h median end-to-end admission for community models, but for enterprise flows we can be slower. Key goals: avoid shipping regressions to serving, keep onboarding throughput >= 20/day for the public pipeline, and keep bench infra cost bounded (not 10x for every candidate).

leila: leaning to a hybrid: a cheap probe stage that runs in <90s and checks basic compatibility + smoke quality signals, then an async heavy bench that runs on a small shard of dedicated GPUs and produces final pass/fail and detailed reports. Probe is a hard pre-ingest gate, heavy bench is soft (can block promotion to 'stable' pool).

leila: example probe checks I'd make required:
- model load + tensor shape sanity
- simple token-level smoke generation (3 prompts) for hallucination spikes
- kv-cache sanity + small memory profile
- signature compatibility (vocab/embedding shape)

leila: quick snippet of probe invocation:

```
# tools/probe.py --fast-probe mode
python tools/probe.py --model $MODEL --inputs tests/smoke_set.json --checks load,shapes,probe-gen --timeout 90
```

yang: interface boundary: probe should return a tiny standardized payload so intake can make deterministic decisions. propose fields: probe_result (pass/fail), probes_run (list), probe_score (0-1), compat_flags (list), meta.hash, kv_cache_ok. Keep schema flat so other systems can easily parse.

marc: storage/cost note — we shouldn't keep full bench outputs for every public model forever. maybe keep probe artifacts indefinitely, but heavy bench artifacts TTL to 30 days unless someone pins. also heavy bench needs to be able to re-run deterministically and reference same seed/inputs.

harper: good point on storage. ops: can we ensure the heavy bench runs on a spot or reserved pool to avoid noisy cost? @infra-bot any ideas?

infra-bot: Scheduling idea: label benches as `bench:fast` vs `bench:full`. `bench:fast` on shared on-demand; `bench:full` on reserved pool (cheaper per-hour) and backfill using spot when available. Quotas per-team to avoid abuse.

leila: another gating thought: keep deterministic model fingerprint (binary + tokenizer hash) in the probe result. if fingerprint differs from registry, block automated rollouts. avoids silent numeric drift regressions.

yang: also add a small quantization-compat check in probe (float32 load -> q8 test inference on a single batch) to surface quant mismatch early. if it fails, fail probe with a clear reason code.

harper: sounds like consensus: make a short required probe (<=90s) that produces a flat JSON of standardized keys, plus an async heavy bench for deeper perf/quality metrics. I'll draft an RFC patch: probe as pre-ingest hard gate, heavy bench as post-ingest validation that can block promotion. I'll include workload-level quotas, artifact TTL, and the schema proposal.

harper: thanks all — will @request reviews when draft is up :+1:
